task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of March 10, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: A worker was struck and killed by an autonomous straddle carrier at the Portside Container Terminal on March 9, 2025, in what federal investigators said is the first fatality at a fully automated container terminal in the United States.
The victim, identified by family as maintenance technician David Osei, 41, was performing a scheduled inspection of a carrier guide rail when the vehicle entered the zone.
The autonomous carrier's proximity detection system had been in a degraded-mode status for approximately 90 minutes before the incident due to a software update deployed that morning.
Portside Terminal director Melissa Ward said: "We have suspended all autonomous vehicle operations pending a full safety review. Our deepest condolences go to the family of our colleague."
The Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an inspection within hours of the incident and has jurisdiction over the investigation of the workplace conditions.
Portside Terminal became fully automated in 2022; the terminal uses 28 autonomous straddle carriers, automated guided vehicles, and remote-operated ship-to-shore cranes.

Terminal records show that the degraded proximity mode was flagged by the terminal's central management system but was not escalated to a stop-work decision; standard protocol allows carriers to continue operating in degraded mode with reduced speed limits.

Paul Kimura, director of the federal Maritime Automation Safety Task Force, said: "We have not had a fatality at a U.S. automated terminal before. This event will force a reassessment of degraded-mode operating permissions at facilities across the country."

A union representing port workers at adjacent non-automated berths said it had raised safety concerns about the Portside expansion to OSHA in 2023; those concerns were addressed in a compliance audit that year.
Portside Terminal handles approximately 1.4 million container units per year; the suspension of autonomous operations has halted roughly 70% of terminal throughput.
The carrier involved is a model manufactured by Helix Automation; the company said it is providing full cooperation to investigators.
Maintenance technicians at Portside are required to use a zone clearance procedure before entering active carrier areas; investigators are examining whether that procedure was followed.
Automated terminals have operated in Europe and Asia since the 1990s; European industry data shows two prior fatalities, both involving temporary workers and human entry into active zones.
Ward said the terminal would not resume autonomous operations until an independent safety audit is complete.
Federal investigators are examining whether the degraded-mode software update should have triggered a mandatory stop-work hold under existing automated equipment regulations.
The Maritime Automation Safety Task Force was established in 2024 but has not yet issued binding standards for automated terminal operations.
Osei's family attorney said the family would pursue all available legal remedies.
Terminal operators' trade group said the industry was committed to working with regulators to update standards in light of the incident.
The autonomous straddle carrier weighs approximately 42 tonnes when unladen.
OSHA has six months to complete its inspection and issue any citations.

forbidden_additions: a finding that the zone clearance procedure was not followed
a criminal charge against Portside or its operators
a claim that the fatality count at automated terminals is higher than stated
